title: Polyglot integration playbooks: retries, streaming ergonomics & minimal examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Provide concise, copy-pasteable reference integrations and "best-practice" playbooks for Python (async), TypeScript (Next.js/Node), and Go (net/http) that showcase: streaming ergonomics, safe retry strategies (idempotent vs non-idempotent), CLI examples for batch jobs, and small cookbook snippets for common pitfalls (prefix caching, cancellation, prompt templating).

Context / Why this exists:
- We get frequent user questions and support tickets about how to: resume/abort streaming responses correctly, implement retries for generation calls, and wire SDKs into common app frameworks (Next.js SSR/Edge, FastAPI ASGI, Go HTTP).
- Existing examples are scattered and either too large or duplicate content in other tickets (starter kits). This ticket is focused on compact, opinionated playbooks that can be referenced from the docs and embedded in Quickstarts.

Deliverables:
1) Next.js (TypeScript) example: a minimal server-side streaming demo using the official TS SDK that demonstrates backpressure, use of ReadableStream/AsyncIterators for streaming tokens, and guidance for ISR vs SSR use cases. Include a small utility for exponential backoff retries for idempotent requests and a clear note for avoiding retries on streaming non-idempotent operations.
2) FastAPI (Python) example: an async endpoint that proxies token stream to clients (EventSource or streaming response), shows how to cancel generation with asyncio cancellation, and includes a simple retry decorator that respects idempotency_token and retries only safe failures (rate-limit, transport).
3) Go HTTP server example: small net/http handler with context-aware generation, examples for setting timeouts via context.WithTimeout, an idempotency-token middleware, and a CLI client that demonstrates chunked streaming consumption.
4) CLI examples: a Python and Go CLI that accept prompt files, stream outputs to stdout, and optionally write to local cache; include --retries, --idempotency-token flags and examples of piping output to other tools.
5) Cookbook snippets: three short copyable snippets (max ~30 lines each) focusing on: (a) retry policy with jitter, (b) safe streaming resume strategy using tokens and offsets, (c) minimal prompt templating with parameter validation.
6) Docs PR: single consolidated docs page linking each example and calling out anti-patterns (blind retries on non-idempotent streamed responses, blocking the event loop on Node, leaking goroutines on cancelled contexts).

Acceptance criteria:
- Each example runs locally with "npm run dev" or "uvicorn app:app --reload" or "go run ./cmd/server" following the README.
- Unit/integration tests for retry behavior (simulated transient errors) included for Python and Go. TS example has a test harness for streaming behavior (jest or playwright smoke test).
- PRs include small demo recordings (mp4 or gif) and CI that runs smoke tests on examples.
- Docs PR merges with cross-links to SDK reference and the console Quickstart where appropriate.

Implementation notes / decisions:
- Retry rules: default policy should retry on transport/fatal HTTP 5xx and 429 with exponential backoff and full jitter. Explicit flag to disable retries for streaming endpoints.
- Idempotency: recommend callers pass an idempotency_token on operations expected to be retried (e.g., non-streamed generation). For streaming responses, prefer short-lived tokens and avoid automatic retries unless client provides an application-level resume token.
- Streaming ergonomics: prefer AsyncIterator/ReadableStream surfaces in SDKs; examples should show both idiomatic and lowest-common-denominator (raw fetch/response.body) approaches.
- Telemetry and debugging: include short guidance on adding Trace-Context headers and correlation ids in examples so developers can match traces with Console.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1 (this ticket): scaffold minimal examples and run local smoke tests. Focus on one canonical pattern per language (TS-Next.js SSR proxy example, Python-FastAPI SSE proxy, Go HTTP chunked handler).
- Week 2: polish retries, add tests, write cookbook snippets and docs PR.
- Week 3: address feedback, record demos, finalize PRs and land.

Attachments / links:
- Design note (draft): https://docs.redwood.example/confluence/sdks/polyglot-playbooks
- Draft PR for TS example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/1203
- Existing example to reuse: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/tree/main/examples/fastapi-proxy

Risks / open questions:
- How to demonstrate resumable streaming in a short example without a large server-side state store? Proposal: demonstrate a stateless resume token pattern (client holds offset and model-side supports resume-from-offset param) with a mocked resume implementation in the example.
- Do we need legal/PII guidance in CLI examples that write outputs to disk? For now add a disclaimer in README and route to Security for higher-risk examples.

Next steps:
- Liam: create feature branches for each language under sdks/examples/polyglot-playbooks and open draft PRs.
- Aisha: write the initial docs draft and checklist for reviewers.
- Assign reviewers: @Sofia Martinez (TS), @Noah Williams (Go), @Priya Rao (Python).
